Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2585); Enoch (i.e. Chanok), an antediluvian:--Enoch.
BiblicalUsage: Enoch stands in Luke's genealogy as the son of Jared in Luke 3:37, and Hebrews tells the rest in Hebrews 11:5: by faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death, because God had translated him, and before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God. Jude adds that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of the Lord coming with ten thousands of His saints in Jude 1:14.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Enoch's life is summed up in one phrase — he pleased God — and his exit from this world without dying is the proof that pleasing God is worth everything. His story lives on his People profile.
